text:
Alex Kim: Hi — setting up a customer-facing demo for tomorrow. My laptop is on corp VPN/proxy so outbound IPs look weird and the sandbox key I'm using keeps hitting rate limits. Should I use a hosted API key for the demo or is there a recommended ephemeral/demo flow?
Maria Chen: For customer demos: avoid hardcoding long-lived hosted keys. Two options: 1) request a short-lived demo key (TTL) from eng-infra, 2) use a sandbox key with a temporary quota bump. If you're behind a proxy, env var proxy is usually enough.
Alex Kim: I don't have session/token APIs in my role yet. Is requesting a temp hosted key the usual path?
Jamie O'Neil: Yup — DM eng-oncall or use the /request-temp-key flow in #eng-infra. We can issue scoped keys with 2-4h TTL and demo-specific rate limits to prevent noise.
Maria Chen: If you go sandbox, ask for a one-off quota increase for the demo window (include exact time + expected QPS). For hosted demo keys we'll tag requests as `project:demo` so finance doesn't get a surprise.
Alex Kim: Quick question — are there proxy env vars or a snippet I can use? Streaming tends to break on our corp proxy.
Maria Chen: Try this for non-websocket streaming (curl chunked):

```
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-demo-xxxxx
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hi"}' \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```
If websocket streaming breaks, fallback to chunked HTTP like above. If you need a websocket demo, SRE can spin up a quick relay in your session.
Jamie O'Neil: Also note: hosted demo keys bill under your org. Ask SRE to set a demo tag `demo-<your-name>`; ops will cap the spend.
devops-bot: Reminder: creating temporary hosted keys requires approval. Use `/request-temp-key` in #eng-infra and reference this thread (1759876543). Approval usually < 30 min during working hours.
Alex Kim: Thanks — I'll open the request now and try the curl flow. Will include expected QPS and times in the request.
Maria Chen: Ping me here once you have the key; I can sanity-check permissions and prompts quickly.
Alex Kim: Will do, thanks :thumbsup:
